# Additions to Esther Chapter 3 (Addition C) — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther C | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_003_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition C: The prayers of Mordecai and Esther. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 4:17. These prayers introduce explicit prayer and divine address into a book that never names God in Hebrew.]*

**1** And Mordecai prayed to the Lord, calling to mind all the works of the Lord, and said:

**2** "O Lord, Lord, King who rules over all, for all things are subject to your power, and there is none who can resist you when it is your will to save Israel.

**3** For you made the heaven and the earth and every wonderful thing under heaven.

**4** You are Lord over all, and there is none who can withstand you, O Lord.

**5** You know all things. You know, Lord, that it was not from insolence or pride or glory-seeking that I acted so — refusing to bow down to the arrogant Haman.

**6** For I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the salvation of Israel.

**7** But I did this so that I might not set the honor of a man above the honor of God; and I will bow down to no one but you, who are my God and Lord; and I will not act out of pride.

**8** And now, O Lord God and King, God of Abraham, have compassion on your people, for their eyes are set on us to destroy us; and they desire to annihilate the inheritance that has been yours from the beginning.

**9** Do not disregard your own portion, which you redeemed for yourself out of the land of Egypt.

**10** Hear my prayer and be merciful to your inheritance; turn our mourning into feasting, that we may live and praise your name, O Lord; and do not close the mouths of those who praise you, O Lord."

**11** And all Israel cried out with great force, for their death was before them.

**12** And Queen Esther, seized with anguish, fled to the Lord.

**13** She removed her splendid garments and put on garments of distress and mourning; in place of the costly perfumes she put ashes and dung on her head, and she greatly humbled her body. Every place she had adorned with joy she filled with the tangles of her unbound hair.

**14** And she prayed to the Lord God of Israel, saying:

**15** "O my Lord, you alone are our King. Help me, who am alone and have no helper but you,

**16** for my danger is imminent.

**17** I have heard from my childhood, in the tribe of my father's family, that you, O Lord, chose Israel from among all the nations, and chose our fathers from among all their forebears as a perpetual inheritance; and you fulfilled for them everything you promised.

**18** But now we have sinned before you, and you have given us into the hands of our enemies

**19** because we glorified their gods. You are righteous, O Lord.

**20** Yet they are not satisfied with the bitterness of our slavery, but have joined their hands with their idols

**21** to abolish the decree of your mouth, to destroy your inheritance, to silence those who praise you, to extinguish the glory of your house and your altar,

**22** and to open the mouths of the nations for the praise of worthless idols and to magnify a mortal king forever.

**23** Do not surrender, O Lord, your scepter to those who have no existence; let them not make sport of our downfall; but turn their counsel against themselves, and make an example of the man who first moved against us.

**24** Remember us, O Lord. Make yourself known in the time of our tribulation, and give me courage, O King of the gods and Master of every dominion.

**25** Put persuasive speech in my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hate the one who fights against us, so that there may be an end of him and of those who agree with him.

**26** But deliver us by your hand, and help me, who am alone and have no helper but you, O Lord.

**27** You have knowledge of all things, and you know that I hate the glory of the lawless and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner.

**28** You know my constraint — that I abhor the sign of my pride that is upon my head on the days when I must appear in public; I abhor it like a cloth of menstruation, and I do not wear it on my days of quiet.

**29** And your servant has not eaten at the table of Haman, and I have not honored the banquet of the king, and I have not drunk the wine of libations.

**30** And your servant has known no joy since the day I was brought here until now, except in you, O Lord God of Abraham.

**31** O God, mighty above all, hear the voice of the despairing, and save us from the hand of the wicked, and deliver me from my fear."
